recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is recommended unless a later separate PA decision requests a new Practitioner.qualification.code binding.
issue_request: The issue requested replacing the example value set for Practitioner.qualification with US provider taxonomy codes, but the Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution directed use of HL7 v2 table 0360 Degree/License/Certificate instead.
initial_application: Commit 8e2188474050f1040164af85bb5382ac2d74059c, whose subject includes Tracker#12659, changed the old Practitioner spreadsheet Qualification binding from valueset-anzsco-occupations to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/v2-2.7-0360 and added a matching v2 table 0360 example coding. Later terminology migration commits d1f387ce5e71114e7369ac9dd345022ded36edd0 and 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 preserved that semantic binding while updating the canonical URL form to http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v2-0360.
additional_context: Practitioner is active in source/fhir.ini, so the current Practitioner StructureDefinition source is in build scope. The current binding at Practitioner.qualification.code has strength example and valueSet http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v2-0360, and the main Practitioner example uses http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/v2-0360/2.7 code BS. Jira search surfaced FHIR-8513 as a duplicate/broader Practitioner.qualification issue, but it was not needed to decide this seed. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting decision.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current active source already implements the final modified resolution, and changing the binding to US taxonomy codes would contradict that resolution.
